subject: How to make MSN look better

messages.author: 1d15a1166a3152c3
messages.subject: How to make MSN look better
parts:
Hello,
I have to say, that poppr is very nice tool, I like it very much. I have several questions regarding look of MSN output. I'm very familiar with igraph and I wonder how to pass it another arguments.
First, is it possible to remove all labels? I'd like to keep only colourful legend, I don't need to display names for individuals nor MLGs. Well, I can do it in some SVG editor later, but... ;-)
Can I change relative size of the circles? E.g make them little bit bigger?
I have relatively big dataset with a lot of haplotypes, so that basic plot looks very ugly. It is full of tiny dots for various haplotypes and labels are so huge and dense, so that I hardly see the network itself. :-) I tried to manipulate with parameters of svg(), but it haven't helped very much.
So how can I make the whole plot bigger? If it contains really plenty of MLGs, the network is huge, circles tiny and labels make it unreadable.
Last problem is related to legend. I have over 60 populations and the legend prints them in very long list, so that exported plot doesn't contain all of them. The only workaround I found was to set in svg() enough high height (after some trials) and subsequently edit output in sVG editor.
Any advice regarding those issues would be appreciated. :-)
Sincerely,
Vojtěch Zeisek

Pokud je tento e-mail součástí obchodního jednání, Přírodovědecká fakulta Univerzity Karlovy v Praze:
a) si vyhrazuje právo jednání kdykoliv ukončit a to i bez uvedení důvodu,
b) stanovuje, že smlouva musí mít písemnou formu,
c) vylučuje přijetí nabídky s dodatkem či odchylkou,
d) stanovuje, že smlouva je uzavřena teprve výslovným dosažením shody na všech náležitostech smlouvy.

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: How to make MSN look better
parts:
Hi Vojtěch,

This question comes up just as I am getting ready to release poppr v.1.1.0. This new version will have a function that will plot the minimum spanning networks created in poppr with a lot more flexibility. This will likely be out next week, but in the mean time, I can address the questions you have now:
First, is it possible to remove all labels?
Yes, it is possible. You can use the argument vertex.label = NA.
Can I change relative size of the circles?

Yes.... kind of. You would have to change it in the igraph object that's returned, change them manually, and then plot it again. For example:
library(poppr)
data(nancycats)

x <- bruvo.msn(nancycats, replen=rep(2, 9), sublist=8:9, vertex.label = NA)
library(igraph)
V(x$graph)$size <- 5
plot(x$graph)
legend('topleft', bty = "n", cex = 0.75, legend = x$populations, title = "Populations", fill = x$colors, border = NULL))
So how can I make the whole plot bigger?
I'm not exactly sure how this would be done. You might attempt to make the dimensions in the call to svg() very large.
Last problem is related to legend. I have over 60 populations and the legend prints them in very long list, so that exported plot doesn't contain all of them.

This one is always tricky. I would recommend plotting it on your own with the code above and then using the legend command in R to create it yourself with the col argument set to something like 3 or 4. 

Cheers,
Zhian
